title: Current and Rivergate
premise: Freya Joubert, a railroad engineer dismissed for refusing to falsify survey reports, is hauling a map of closed lines and a compass she inherited from a father who vanished upriver years ago. When a dying prospector named Aldous Wren trades her a second map — one showing the forbidden source of the Current River and a cache of unregistered silver — for a promise to see his claim honored, Freya and her estranged half-brother Tomas, a Rivergate company clerk who once betrayed her, are pulled into a race against expiring concession permits. Pursued by the company's enforcer, Silas Crane, and guided by a disgraced river pilot named Odile Marchand, they discover the source hides not treasure but proof that Rivergate's founder stole the silver rights from Freya's father, whose bones rest beside it. In the end, Freya chooses truth over the fortune: she surrenders the silver to Wren's daughter and publishes her father's survey, collapsing the concession and reclaiming her name, though it costs her the river she has come to love.
about_author: Sable Ravensworth is the pen name of a former land surveyor who spent a decade mapping waterways across the northern territories before turning to fiction. They write adventure novels about people who measure the world honestly and pay for it.

chapters.title: The Weight of Closed Lines
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. In the rail town of Verrin's Crossing, Freya is dismissed from the survey corps after refusing to sign falsified grades for a Rivergate spur line. Packing her father's compass and her map of closed lines, she learns her debt to the company is being called in within thirty days. The beat is quiet defiance masking fear.

chapters.title: A Dying Man's Bargain
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. On the road out of town she finds Aldous Wren, a prospector shot and left for dead by men wearing Rivergate badges. He trades her a wax-cloth map of the Current River's forbidden source for a sworn promise: deliver his claim papers to his daughter in Rivergate before the concession permits expire in six weeks. The beat is reluctant oath-taking.

chapters.title: Half-Blood at the Company Desk
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. In Rivergate city, Tomas Joubert — Freya's half-brother, raised legitimate while she was not — processes permit renewals and discovers the Current concession expires on the same date Wren named. Ordered by Silas Crane to intercept a 'thieving woman with a map,' he recognizes the description. The beat is dread of an old betrayal repeating.

chapters.title: The Pilot Who Drowned
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya hires Odile Marchand, a river pilot officially listed as dead after she refused to run company barges through a flood that killed eleven men. Odile agrees to take her upstream only as far as the Splits. The beat is wary alliance between two women the company has erased.

chapters.title: Permits and Knives
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas files a false travel manifest to buy Freya three days of lead time, then lies to Crane about her direction. Crane, unconvinced, requisitions the company steamer Perpetual and a crew of enforcers. The beat is Tomas discovering he can still choose, and hating how small the choice is.

chapters.title: Upstream Against the Current
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The shallow-draft boat fights the Current's rapids; Odile teaches Freya to read water the way she reads grades and gradients. At night Freya overlays Wren's map on her father's closed lines and finds they share a datum point — her father surveyed the source first. The beat is wonder curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Splits
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. At the river's fork, Odile reveals her debt: her brother was one of the eleven drowned, and the company paid her to stay silent. Crane's steamer appears downstream, forcing a choice — the legal channel or the dead pilot's shortcut through the gorge. The beat is guilt converted into resolve.

chapters.title: Brother Against the Water
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Crane, suspicious of Tomas's errors, takes him aboard the Perpetual as insurance. Tomas sabotages a boiler gauge to slow the pursuit, nearly killing everyone aboard, and realizes Crane expected the sabotage and let it happen to bind him. The beat is horror at becoming a weapon.

chapters.title: The Gorge of Names
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. In the gorge, the party finds prospectors' graves, each marked with a name scratched into slate — including Joubert. Freya confronts the possibility her father reached the source and was silenced. Odile admits the river has a second, unmapped channel. The beat is grief arriving ahead of proof.

chapters.title: Wren's Daughter
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A supply stop at the mission town of Saint-Aubin lets Freya send Wren's claim papers onward — but Crane's agents intercept the mail rider. Freya learns the papers are now bait to lure her into the open. The beat is the promise becoming a trap she must still keep.

chapters.title: What the Compass Points To
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Her father's compass, tested against Wren's map, doesn't point north at the datum — it points along a bearing only a surveyor would recognize, a line her father hid inside his closed-line maps. Freya deciphers it: the true source lies off every chart, behind a limestone shelf. The beat is inheritance understood at last.

chapters.title: The Perpetual Gains
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The repaired steamer closes the gap. Crane offers Tomas full reinstatement and their father's old house if he delivers Freya alive. Tomas sees the offer for what it is — the same bargain their father took — and jumps ship at night into the gorge. The beat is choosing exile over inheritance.

chapters.title: Reunion in the Rapids
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Tomas, half-drowned, is pulled aboard by Odile. The siblings' confrontation is raw: he took the legitimate name, the schooling, the house; she took the compass and the debt. They do not forgive each other, but they agree on the bearing. The beat is loyalty re-forged without absolution.

chapters.title: Crane's Ledger
chapters.summary: Crane's POV. Crane burns the mission's mail room to destroy Wren's papers, revealing to the reader (not the heroes) that he carries his own ledger — proof he was the man who shot Wren and, decades ago, escorted Joubert senior upriver. The beat is a villain who believes he is closing old accounts, not starting crimes.

chapters.title: The Limestone Shelf
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Following the compass bearing through the second channel, the party finds the shelf and the hidden cleft behind it. The river's forbidden source is a spring-fed cavern system, and the water is silver-bright with ore dust. The beat is awe — the map was true, and that is the terrifying part.

chapters.title: Bones and Surveys
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. In the cavern they find her father's camp, his final survey, and his remains. His journal proves Rivergate's founder stole the silver rights via a forged concession, with Crane as witness. Tomas, arriving breathless, confirms the permit expiry is in four days. The beat is truth as both vindication and burden.

chapters.title: The Stand at the Source
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Crane's party reaches the cavern mouth. A standoff in the dark: Crane offers Freya the fortune if she burns the journal; Tomas turns Crane's own ledger evidence against him; Odile floods the lower passage by breaching a sluice her brother helped build. The beat is every debt called at once.

chapters.title: The River Takes Its Due
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The flood drives Crane's crew out but traps Freya and Tomas in the inner cavern with the water rising. Freya, engineer to the last, calculates an escape through the ore fissures while the journal — copied in Tomas's clerk's hand — is sealed in oilcloth against her chest. The beat is trust tested at flood level.

chapters.title: Four Days to Rivergate
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The survivors race downstream, Odile running water she swore never to run again, to beat the permit expiry and reach Wren's daughter and the assayer's office before Crane can file a salvage claim on the cavern. The beat is the river, once an obstacle, becoming their ally.

chapters.title: The Reading of the Claims
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. In Rivergate, before the permit board, Freya surrenders the silver to Wren's daughter per her oath and reads her father's journal and Crane's ledger into the record. The concession collapses; Crane is taken by his own company's lawyers. The beat is truth winning not by force but by being spoken on time.

chapters.title: What Freya Kept
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya declines the company's offer to lead a new, honest survey of the Current. Instead she takes the closed-lines map, now hers by right, and a contract from Wren's daughter to survey the silver claim fairly. Tomas asks to come. The beat is inheritance redefined as work, not treasure.

chapters.title: The Source, Measured
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, epilogue. A year later, Freya and Tomas, with Odile piloting, complete the first honest survey of the Current from mouth to source, setting the datum stone at the spring beside their father's marked grave. The compass, finally pointing true north, is left on the stone. The beat is peace earned by telling the truth all the way upstream.
